cohort: 250 females undergoing cesarean section at term.
finding: The study concluded that amoxicillin was more effective than ceftriaxone in preventing post-operative wound infection after cesarean section, despite the observed difference (1.6% vs 6.4%) being statistically insignificant (p=0.053).
mod_finding: The study found that amoxicillin was more effective than ceftriaxone in preventing wound infection following cesarean section.
